name: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArafa al-Azdī al-ʿAtakī
summary: Baghdad grammarian and historian, a student of Thaʿlab and al-Mubarrad, whose nickname joins 'naphtha' to the ending of Sībawayh's name.
bio: Nifṭawayh was born in Wāsiṭ and taught in Baghdad; he learnt from Thaʿlab and al-Mubarrad and followed the Ẓāhirī school in law. The sources explain his nickname as 'naphtha' (for his dark skin) joined to the ending of Sībawayh's name, since he followed Sībawayh in grammar; al-Zubaydī nevertheless lists him among Thaʿlab's companions in the sixth Kufan generation.
He was also a historian and a teacher of hadith, and taught the Qurʾān for fifty years in the same mosque. Al-Qālī was among his students. He died in 323/935.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 80 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
